title: E Line Opening
description: The E Line (Expo) opened between 7th/Metro Center and Culver City, LA Metro's first new light rail line in over a decade.

title: L Line Azusa Extension
description: The L Line (Gold) extended from Azusa Avenue to Downtown Azusa and APU/Citrus College, adding six new stations in the San Gabriel Valley.

title: E Line Extended to Santa Monica
description: The E Line (Expo) extended from Culver City to Downtown Santa Monica, completing the full Expo Line corridor from downtown LA to the coast.

title: COVID-19 Service Reductions
description: LA Metro reduced service system-wide in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Ridership dropped dramatically and recovery has been gradual.

title: COVID-19 Emergency Schedule
description: From April 19, 2020 every Metro bus and train ran a modified Sunday schedule seven days a week. Rail operated every 12 minutes from about 6am to 6pm and every 20 minutes at all other times; weekday bus service was the usual Sunday schedule plus a handful of Rapid, Express and local lines that do not normally run on Sundays.

title: NextGen Bus Plan Phase 1
description: The first of three NextGen service changes took effect December 13, 2020, opening Metro's first full bus-network redesign in more than 25 years. Trips were added on many lines to improve frequency, routes were modified to speed up trips, and a few low-ridership lines were discontinued.

title: Rapid Lines Retired into Local Service
description: NextGen Phase 1 consolidated eight Metro Rapid lines into their partner locals: 705 into 105, 710 into 210, 728 into 28, 740 into 40 and 210, 745 into 45, 751 into 251, 760 into 60 and 762 into 260. The locals absorbed those riders on more frequent service, and selected stops were dropped to recover part of the Rapid travel-time advantage.

title: NextGen Bus Plan Phase 2
description: The largest NextGen phase took effect June 27, 2021: 70 bus lines gained trips every day of the week (the G Line among them), 23 more on weekdays (including the J Line), 4 on Saturdays and 1 on Sundays, with stop consolidation on 8 lines and added weekday peak rail service on the A, C, E and L Lines.

title: GoPass Free Student Fares Launch
description: Metro launched the GoPass pilot in October 2021, giving K-14 students across LA County an unlimited free transit pass and the first phase of its Fareless System Initiative. By April 2023 more than 100 school districts and 1,400 schools had joined, and registered students had made 16.6 million boardings.

title: NextGen Bus Plan Phase 3
description: The third and final NextGen service change landed in December 2021, completing the network restructure. Metro's own assessment a year later found 2.2 million more people living within a quarter mile of 10-minute-or-better weekday midday service — an increase of more than 700%.

title: K Line Opening
description: The K Line (Crenshaw/LAX) opened between Expo/Crenshaw and Westchester/Veterans stations, serving the Crenshaw corridor and Inglewood.

title: Bus Service Restored to Pre-Pandemic Levels
description: On December 11, 2022 Metro restored bus service to full pre-pandemic levels, adding 300,000 revenue service hours back into the network for a total of 7 million annualized hours, with NextGen frequency improvements across the system.

title: Regional Connector Opening
description: The Regional Connector linked the A, C, E, and L lines through a new downtown tunnel, creating through-running service and eliminating transfers at 7th/Metro. Ridership figures for these lines were significantly restructured as a result.

title: L Line Discontinued
description: The Regional Connector absorbed the L Line (Gold) into the A and E Lines: the Azusa branch became the A Line's northern half and the East LA branch became the E Line's eastern half. The L Line ceased to exist as a route, which is why it reports no ridership from July 2023 onward.

title: B/D Line Subway Frequency Increase
description: From September 10, 2023 the B and D Line subways ran every 12 minutes instead of every 15 for most of the day — weekdays about 6am to 9pm, weekends 8:15am to 7pm — giving the shared Union Station–Wilshire/Vermont trunk a train every 6 minutes. Metro framed the increase as part of restoring service to pre-pandemic levels.

title: A/E Line Frequency and Late-Night Increase
description: From December 10, 2023 the A and E Lines ran every 8 minutes at peak instead of every 10, and every 10 minutes midday and on weekends instead of every 12. Two extra trains per direction extended nightly service by about 40 minutes — the last A Line trains leave Azusa and Downtown Long Beach at 11:45pm, and the last E Line trains leave Santa Monica at 11:54pm and East LA at 12:18am.

title: C and K Lines Reconfigured at Aviation/Century
description: On November 3, 2024 the new Aviation/Century station opened and the two lines were re-cut around it: the C Line ran Norwalk to Aviation/Century, while the K Line ran Expo/Crenshaw to Westchester/Veterans and, separately, Aviation/Century to Redondo Beach. Riders using Mariposa, El Segundo, Douglas or Redondo Beach now changed between the two lines at Aviation/Century. Both changes were temporary, pending the LAX/Metro Transit Center opening.

title: December 2024 Service Changes
description: Schedule changes took effect December 15, 2024, adding trips on some lines and reconfiguring others to improve connections to Metro rail. Line 96 became Line 296, terminating at the Lincoln/Cypress A Line station; Line 260 was split into two routes, 260 to Willowbrook/Rosa Parks and a new 261 to Artesia; and Lines 177 and 256 transferred to Pasadena Transit as Routes 53 and 33.

title: D Line Closed for 70 Days
description: The entire D Line shut down from May 17, 2025 for 70 days so crews could tie the existing subway into the Section 1 extension tunnels west of Wilshire/Western. Shuttle buses replaced trains between Wilshire/Western and Wilshire/Vermont.

title: LAX/Metro Transit Center Opens
description: The LAX/Metro Transit Center station opened June 6, 2025 on the C and K Lines, closing the rail gap between Aviation/Century and Westchester/Veterans that had existed since the K Line debuted in 2022 and completing the K Line's initial phase.

title: D Line Service Resumes
description: D Line trains started running again on July 26, 2025 after the 70-day closure, ahead of the Section 1 extension opening. Trains ran every 12 minutes from 9am to 8pm.

title: A Line Foothill Extension to Pomona
description: The A Line opened nine miles and four stations east to Pomona on September 19, 2025 — Glendora, San Dimas, La Verne and Pomona. Already the longest light rail line in the world since the 2023 Blue/Gold merge, it now runs 57.6 miles from Pomona to Long Beach.

title: D Line Section 1 Extension
description: The D Line (Purple) extended westward from Wilshire/Western to three new Westside stations: Wilshire/La Brea, Wilshire/Fairfax, and Wilshire/La Cienega.
